issues.t: Engine knocking, power loss or sudden engine failure
issues.sym: A knock or loud bang from the engine, a "reduced engine power" message, stalling, or the engine quitting while you drive. In the worst cases oil pours out under the car.
issues.why: Owners in a 2026 class-action lawsuit say the 1.2L three-cylinder used in the Envista, Trax, Trailblazer and Encore GX can wear out its connecting-rod bearings and break a rod, sometimes punching a hole in the engine block. GM has not issued a recall, and the claims have not been proven.
issues.next: If you hear a new knock or get a reduced-power message, pull over safely and do not keep driving. Have it towed to a Buick dealer while it is under warranty, keep every service record, and stay on top of oil changes with the correct dexos oil.

issues.t: Smoke or fire from under the hood
issues.sym: Smoke, a burning smell, popping or crackling sounds, or flames from the engine area, sometimes while driving on the highway.
issues.why: Owners have reported engine fires to NHTSA for every Envista model year so far. The engine-failure lawsuit says that when a connecting rod breaks through the block, leaking oil can land on hot exhaust parts and catch fire. The exact cause of each fire is not confirmed.
issues.next: If you see smoke or flames, pull over, turn the engine off, get everyone out and away from the car, and call 911. Do not open the hood. If you notice burning smells or oil leaks, get the car checked before driving it again.

issues.sym: The digital gauge screen goes black at startup or while driving, so you can't see your speed or warning lights.
issues.why: A software fault in the Virtual Cockpit Unit module that runs the gauge display. GM recall 23V744000 covers about 60,000 2024 Envista, Encore GX and Trax models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls on NHTSA's site or with a Buick dealer. The fix is a free software update, sometimes sent over the air.

issues.t: Gauges and center screen go dark or freeze
issues.sym: The speedometer, gauges or the touchscreen go blank, flicker or freeze while driving, for a few seconds or for minutes. It may keep happening after a dealer visit.
issues.why: Display blackouts are the most common NHTSA complaint for the 2024 and 2025 Envista. Some happen on cars the recall software did not cover; dealers often cannot make the fault happen in the shop.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Note when it happens and take a phone video, since that helps the dealer. Make sure all recall and software updates are done. If the gauges go out while driving, keep to the flow of traffic, pull over when it is safe, and restart the car. You can't see warning lights while the screen is dark, so get it repaired under warranty.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the rearview camera picture is blank, distorted or foggy.
issues.why: A faulty rear camera. GM recall 26V539000 covers 2024-2025 Envista and related small GM SUVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Until it is fixed, check mirrors and look over your shoulder when backing up. Dealers replace the camera free once parts are available.

issues.t: Backup camera dark or grainy in low light
issues.sym: The rearview picture works in daylight but is too dark, grainy or cuts out at night or in a garage.
issues.why: GM bulletin 23-NA-169 says some early cameras perform poorly in low light and calls for camera replacement.
issues.next: Ask a Buick dealer to check the camera against bulletin 23-NA-169 and the camera recall. Use your mirrors carefully when backing up at night.

issues.t: Brake warning lights and loss of braking
issues.sym: Several brake or ABS warnings light up at once, the pedal feels wrong, or the car does not stop as it should, sometimes at low speed.
issues.why: Owners of 2024, 2025 and 2026 Envistas have reported sudden brake warnings and reduced braking to NHTSA. Repairs reported include the brake control module, master cylinder and brake booster. No recall has been issued.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard, press it much harder than normal. If it sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If brake warnings come on or the pedal feels different, stop as soon as it is safe and have the car towed. Do not drive with a brake warning light on.

issues.t: Check engine light from evaporative (EVAP) system faults
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with a fuel smell, and a code scan shows an EVAP or fuel vapor code.
issues.why: The fuel vapor system uses an electric purge pump that GM has bulletins on (23-NA-214). Owners also report leaking filler pipes and fuel vapor codes that come back after repair.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks shut. If the light stays on, have the codes read. If it is steady and the car runs normally, it is usually not urgent, but get it fixed so you pass emissions and don't miss another problem. A flashing light means pull over.

issues.t: Oil burning and blue smoke from a failed camshaft cover
issues.sym: Blue smoke from the tailpipe and the oil level dropping quickly, even on a low-mileage car.
issues.why: GM bulletin PIP5947A says the camshaft (valve) cover, which has the crankcase ventilation parts built in, can fail and let the engine pull oil into the intake.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and top it off. Running low on oil can damage this engine, so take it to a Buick dealer and mention bulletin PIP5947A.

issues.t: Oil leak from a porous cylinder head
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the side of the engine or drops under the car, with no loose part to blame.
issues.why: Tiny pores in the aluminum cylinder head casting can let oil seep through. GM bulletin 23-NA-122 gives a sealing repair so the engine does not have to be replaced.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level and have the leak checked under warranty. Mention bulletin 23-NA-122.

issues.t: Check engine light with codes P0324 or P0116
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, but the car drives normally.
issues.why: Engine computer software could set false knock sensor (P0324) or coolant temperature (P0116) codes. GM bulletin 24-NA-064 calls for reprogramming.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If they match, a dealer software update should fix it under warranty.

issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine, or the whole car, shuts off while moving, sometimes at highway speed. Steering gets heavy.
issues.why: Owners have reported sudden shutdowns to NHTSA. Some are linked to the engine problems above, and others were never traced by the dealer.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Steer to the side of the road with firm effort and use the brakes firmly. Do not keep driving a car that has stalled. Have it towed and ask the dealer to check stored codes and engine condition.

issues.t: Roof water leak and key fob not working
issues.sym: Water drips inside near the roof or headliner, and the key fob or remote locks may stop working.
issues.why: GM bulletin 23-NA-107 links a roof water leak to wet electronics, including the remote door lock receiver.
issues.next: Dry out the cabin and get it to the dealer soon, because water can damage wiring and cause mold. Mention bulletin 23-NA-107.

issues.sym: The touchscreen freezes, reboots, loses audio, or phone projection drops out.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins on radio software (23-NA-145) and a later update with center display fixes (A23-241580).
issues.next: Accept over-the-air updates when the car offers them. If it keeps happening, ask the dealer to install the latest radio software.

issues.sym: A "Service Front Camera" message comes and goes, and lane keeping or automatic braking may stop working for a while.
issues.why: GM bulletin 23-NA-204 covers this message showing up on and off. The windshield camera runs several safety features.
issues.next: Keep the windshield clean in front of the camera. If the message keeps coming back, have the dealer check it, and don't count on lane keeping or auto braking until it is fixed.

issues.sym: One or more windows won't go up or down, or work only now and then.
issues.why: GM released a diagnostic guide (PIC6523) for power windows that stop working on these models.
issues.next: If a window is stuck down, protect the cabin from rain and have the dealer check the switch, motor and wiring under warranty.

issues.t: Loose door pillar or window trim
issues.sym: Exterior trim on the door pillars or around the rear side windows lifts, rattles or comes off, often after a car wash.
issues.why: GM bulletin 23-NA-179 covers loose B-pillar trim, and 2025 owners report rear window trim detaching.
issues.next: Push it back on if you can and avoid automatic car washes until the dealer reattaches or replaces it under warranty.

issues.sym: The wireless charging pad stops charging certain newer iPhones.
issues.why: GM bulletin PIT6097C says some iPhone 15 software versions don't work with the charger and the fix is a phone update.
issues.next: Update your phone's software first. If it still won't charge, have the dealer check the charging module.
